text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGE: continuous-batching scheduler alerted — sudden latency cliff + KV cache growth in us-west-2. route: /v1/generate. 95p latency jumped ~120ms -> ~1.2s, error rate +3%. paging oncall (auto-alert).
tess: acked, joining. what signals do we have so far? any customer hits called out?
maya: kv cache size ramping on nodes cb-*-usw2, eviction rate spiking. traffic qps roughly normal but observed microbatch size spike to 32 for some request patterns. looks like kvcache allocations exploded.
sam: FYI: prefetch heuristic change landed yesterday (PR #2123). rolling back that heuristic is on the short list. checking rollout timeline and which pools saw the new code.
lee: severity bump — 3 enterprise customers reported timeouts, one says user-facing errors. I'm escalating CS and CCing account lead.
maya: quick dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.local/d/cont-batch/kv-growth?from=now-15m — kvcache bytes curve looks like a step function around 01:44 UTC.
sam: logs snippet from cb-3:
```json
{"ts":"2026-03-15T01:45:12Z","node":"cb-3","kvcache_size":124567890,"microbatch":32,"evictions_per_min":980}
```
tess: mitigation options: 1) reduce max_microbatch on affected pool 2) apply backpressure/throttle to prefetch loop 3) quick revert of prefetched multiplier (PR 2123) if rollout is identified. Which is least risky and fastest?
alin: I can apply a config hotfix to lower max_microbatch and disable aggressive prefetch. e.g. PATCH /config/pools/cb-usw2 {"max_microbatch":8, "prefetch_enabled":false}.
jordan: I'll run the canary patch then promote. prepping the commands now.
jordan:
```bash
# canary patch
curl -X PATCH https://config-api.prod/internal/pools/cb-usw2 -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"max_microbatch":8}'
# check scheduler logs for microbatch adjustment
kubectl logs deployment/cb-scheduler -n prod -l pool=cb-usw2 | tail -n 200
```
maya: canary applied to cb-3. immediate effect — kvcache growth rate dropped, eviction rate down ~70% within 45s. microbatch histogram shows shift back to 6-8.
lee: letting affected customer know we've applied mitigation; reported latency improvements on their end.
tess: rolling to prod in staggered fashion — 10s between nodes. jordan, you own rollout. call out if metrics diverge.
jordan: rolling... node cb-1 done -> cb-2 done -> cb-3 done -> cb-4 done. post-rollout metrics: 95p latency ~160ms (near baseline). error rate back to normal.
incident-bot: :white_check_mark: mitigation applied. please prepare handoff notes and RCA next steps.
tess: handoff for night team — monitor prefetched_bytes, kvcache_size and microbatch histogram. if kvcache size > baseline * 1.5 or microbatch median > 12, page oncall-senior. Also watch allocation churn.
sam: filing incident ticket INC-2026-045. probable root cause: prefetch multiplier regression that scaled with concurrency, causing microbatch amplification and runaway kvcache allocations. starting rollback PR and a safer backoff heuristic (cap + linear backoff).
maya: RCA to-do: capture traces for impacted requests, snapshot KV cache for affected nodes, annotate with customer request IDs. add a load-gen test to reproduce high-concurrency prefetch behavior.
tess: quick post-incident checklist: 1) confirm rollback PR and canary plan 2) add metric alert for microbatch median and kvcache growth slope 3) update release notes to call out prefetch heuristic risk.
ops-bot: Note: rollback window scheduled; target SHA abc123 to be reverted per sam.
sam: TODOs: open PR to revert 2123, add guardrail in prefetch logic, run integration load test simulating 10k concurrent sessions.
tess: thanks all — closing pager. I'll post a short blameless summary in #incidents and link INC-2026-045. moving follow-ups to the postincident RCA thread. :heart:
